blocks: Is there a way to make yazi display files differently based on the gitignore status?
The plugin runs git status --porcelain --ignored=matching and displays a badge next to each file. Gitignored files get a darkgray foreground by default (via the !! porcelain prefix).
Is there a way to make yazi display files differently based on the gitignore status?
Is there a way to make yazi display files differently based on the gitignore status?

Caveat — fd hides gitignored files by default: yazi uses fd for directory listing and fd itself respects .gitignore, so gitignored files won't appear in the listing at all unless you configure yazi to show them. There is no built-in show_gitignored toggle; the workaround is to pass --no-ignore to fd via manager config or to accept that the badge only shows up on files fd does list. See issue #1655 for context (closed as not planned).

Yazzi is almost certainly yazi (the Rust terminal file manager).
Using yazi, how do I move a file from one location to another?

Move to another folder: select the entry (Space, or use visual mode v), press x to yank (cut), navigate to the target directory (h / j / k / l or arrows), then p to paste. That moves the file or directory from the source path to the destination.

Copy instead of move: y (copy yank), move the cursor to the destination, p to paste.
Using yazi, how do I move a file from one location to another?
If a same-named file already exists: P (shift+p) pastes with overwrite; plain p avoids overwriting by renaming (suffix such as _1) per default behavior.
